subject: Data as sum of two variables; Bayesian belief model

messages.author: 90b5ae7e2259370d
messages.subject: Data as sum of two variables; Bayesian belief model
parts:
Dear all,

I’m trying to fit an ‘optimal observer’ model for a human learning task (psychology) in which each of my data samples is the sum of two normal processes. Specifically in the task, there are 2 players on each trial working together to produce one summed outcome, by playing 1 of 2 games (stimuli). In total there are 3 agents (out of which 2 are playing on each round). Each agent has for each game a pay-off drawn from a normal distribution. The pay offs from the two players are averaged together. Overall there are 60 rounds. I am trying to build a model that tells me the most likely parameters for each agent for each stimulus, given data observed so far (for example, what is the most likely values for an agent after I have observed 2 rounds, what about after 20 rounds?).

The model is:

data{
  int mtr;             // trials (=rounds) per block
  int nstim;           // number of stimuli per block
  int nplayers;         // number of agents per block -1
  int stims[mtr];  // stim on each trial
  int players[mtr,2]; // players on each trial
  vector[mtr] outs;  // magnitude outcome on each trial - is rounded to integer
}

transformed data{
  vector[mtr] outs2;
  outs2 <-outs*2; // this is to deal with the fact that ‘outs’ is the average of the two players

}

parameters{
  real<lower=-6,upper=6> parasMt[mtr,nplayers+1,nstim]; // trial specific estimates  /1=bls
  real<lower=0,upper=1>  parasSDt[mtr,nplayers+1,nstim]; //very narrow range for now to see whether it runs, should change later?
  vector<lower=-1,upper=1>[mtr] roundError; // rounding error is max. 0.5, but outs2 is 2*outs, so also have to double the error
}

transformed parameters{
  vector[mtr] outsR;
  outsR<-outs2-roundError;
}

model{
  int cstim;
  int cplay1;
  int cplay2;

  // Priors
  roundError ~ normal(0,10);
  for (it in 1:mtr){
    for (ip in 1:3){
      parasMt[it,ip,:]  ~ normal(0,10);
      parasSDt[it,ip,:] ~ normal(0,10); 
    }}
  
  // Model 
    for (t in 1:mtr){
      for (i in 1:t){
        cstim    <- stims[i];
        cplay1   <- players[i,1];
        cplay2   <- players[i,2];
        outsR[i] ~ normal(parasMt[t,cplay1,cstim]+parasMt[t,cplay2,cstim],sqrt(parasSDt[t,cplay1,cstim]^2+parasSDt[t,cplay2,cstim]^2));
      }
    }
}


1) When I try to sample this, it does not converge (even with 2000 samples each for burnin and sampling). However, when I make a variant of the model that only tells me the belief in the last round, it does converge (with 500,500 samples). It seems to me like the model above which models a parameter estimate for each trial should be running in the same way? The model with only the belief for the last round is:
parameters{
  real<lower=-6,upper=6> parasMt[nplayers+1,nstim]; // trial specific estimates  /1=bls
  real<lower=0,upper=1>  parasSDt[nplayers+1,nstim]; //very narrow range for now to see whether it runs, should cahnge later?
  vector<lower=-1,upper=1>[mtr] roundError; // rounding error is max. 0.5, but outs2 is 2*outs, so also have to double the error
}

transformed parameters{
  vector[mtr] outsR;
  outsR<-outs2-roundError;
}

model{
  int cstim;
  int cplay1;
  int cplay2;

  // Model 
    for (t in 1:mtr){
        cstim    <- stims[t];
        cplay1   <- players[t,1];
        cplay2   <- players[t,2];
        outsR[t] ~ normal(parasMt[cplay1,cstim]+parasMt[cplay2,cstim],sqrt(parasSDt[cplay1,cstim]^2+parasSDt[cplay2,cstim]^2));
    }
}

2) There is a warning when compiling the model and I’m sorry I don’t understand from reading the manual whether this may be causing the problem: “compile: Warning (non-fatal): Left-hand side of sampling statement (~) may contain a non-linear transform of a parameter or local variable. If so, you need to call increment_log_prob() with the log absolute determinant of the Jacobian of the transform. Left-hand-side of sampling statement:  outsR[i] ~ normal(…)”
I’m not sure whether this is maybe related to the way I’m trying to add up two randomly drawn values? I also tried coding this as 
outsR[t] ~ outsR[i] ~  normal(parasMt[t,cplay1,cstim],parasSDt[t,cplay1,cstim]) + normal(parasMt[t,cplay2,cstim],parasSDt[t,cplay2,cstim]); 
but this didn’t even compile

3) It’s only on trial 6 that each combination of stimulus and player has occurred at least once (see temp.data.R) and obviously not each parameter affect each trial; I am not sure whether that might be causing problem? (but i’m giving each variable a prior which I thought would prevent this being a problem?


I would greatly appreciate any help with this.
Jacquie

parts:
Dear all,

I have maybe figured it out (at least it is now converging and the estimated parameters are sensible - it recovers the parameters that made the simulated data) - the problem was with how I was trying to do the rounding. The data is integer values only - I had tried to solve this as described in this post https://groups.google.com/forum/#!searchin/stan-users/rounding_latent%7Csort:relevance/stan-users/KIH26xC_3UM/nlJ0TV6ZBgAJ in the ‘rounding_latent’ script. However, I think this does not work in my case; I’m not sure why (maybe because of how i’m sampling in i and in t for outsR?). I have tried to address this now by setting the the type for ‘outs’ and ‘outs2’ to integer. The relevant code is:
data{ 
  int outs[mtr];
}
transformed data{
  int outs2[mtr];//vector[mtr] outs2;
  for (i in 1:mtr){
    outs2[i] <-outs[i]*2;}
}
model{

// Model 
    for (t in 1:mtr){
      for (i in 1:t){
        cstim    <- stims[i];
        cplay1   <- players[i,1];
        cplay2   <- players[i,2];

outs2[i] ~ normal(parasMt[t,cplay1,cstim]+parasMt[t,cplay2,cstim],sqrt(parasSDt[t,cplay1,cstim]^2+parasSDt[t,cplay2,cstim]^2));
      }}}

Is this the right way to solve the rounding problem?
